translations.title: Conversation
translations.text:
You dead seldom manage
to have freedom, but the night
you return is yours,
entirely yours.

My beloved, my remorse,

la nuit c’est toi when I am alone
and you return, you begin
to recognize me in your portraits.

What hurt does your smile remind me of?
And which hardness of mine is in your eyes?
Do you comfort me because I was close
to you at some moment?

The part of your death I assign myself,
the part of your death that I contributed,
how can I repay you for it...
Not even with the part of life we shared.

How can I know you have forgiven me,
alone with you at the scene of the crime?
How can I sleep while you shiver
in the saddest corner of my room?
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Past the Summit of Life...
translations.text:
Past the summit of life,
just on the other side, I contemplate
a landscape not without beauty
on sunny days, but inhospitable in winter.
Here it would be sweet to build the house
I had no need of in other climates,
learning to be chaste and to be alone.
Wisdom is a way of living.
And what a purified shiver
would pass through me
as I attended to the world
in another, better, less intense way,
and in the quiet hours of night,
when time invites noble studies,
pondered the stern discourse of ideologies
—or the warning of the constellations
in the blue vault...
Though the pleasure of abstract thought
is like every pleasure:
a realm of youth.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Love More Powerful Than Life
translations.text:
The same quality as the sun of your country
emerging from the clouds:
a cheerful, delicate shade upon leaves,
a glint of glass, a modulation
of the rain's muted gleam.

The same quality as your city,
your city of countless panes of glass,
the same yet different, changed by time:
streets I do not know and the old square
filled with birds,
the square where we kissed one night.

The same quality as your expression
after all these years,
looking at me tonight:
the same quality as your expression
and the wounded expression of your lips.

Love with the quality of life,
love without demands on the future,
the present of the past,
love more powerful than life:
lost and found.
Found, lost...
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Hours Have Not Yet Passed...
translations.text:
The hours have not yet passed,
and this morning lies far away like a reef
I can barely make out.

You do not feel
how time thickens in this room
with the light on, how the cold outside
licks the windowpanes... How quickly,
in my bed tonight, little creature,
with the simple dignity of need,
while I watched you, you fell asleep.

So, good night.
That peaceful country
whose borders follow the shape of your body
makes one want to die remembering life,
or to stay awake
—tired and excited—until dawn.

Alone with age while you sleep
like someone who has never read a book,
little creature: human being
—more candid than in my arms—
through the unknown.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: The Familiar Streets Receive Us
translations.text:
The familiar streets receive us
and the afternoon already underway; the weary
chestnut trees whose leaves obediently
roll beneath the feet of one returning
go before and accompany our steps.
Breaking into the crowd
of those who succeed one another at every instant,
beneath the premature opacity
of the sky, nearing its end,
each forgetfully retreats,
lost in solitary quarters
of the coming winter. Do you remember
the skill of birds in flight,
the joy and dangerous games,
the intensity of a certain moment, still
beneath a sky higher than the foliage?
If only someone remembered,
if someone suddenly seized by it
remembered... The worn light leaves
butterfly dust between our fingers.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Poetic Art
translations.text:
Longing for the sun on the rooftops,
on the dove-colored concrete wall
—so vivid nonetheless—and the sudden cold
that almost takes one's breath away.

The sweetness, the warmth of lips alone
in the middle of the familiar street,
like a great drawing room where distant crowds
might gather as though they were loved ones.

And above all the vertigo of time,
the great hole opening inward in the soul
while above it promises float,
fainting like foam.

This is surely the moment to think
that being alive demands something,
perhaps heroic deeds—or is it enough,
simply, to take some humble common thing,

its crust of earthly matter,
in one's fingers, with a little faith?
Words, for example.
Familiar words, worn warm by use.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: To a Very Young Lady, Separated
translations.text:
In the year you were
married, beautiful breasts,
you found the flowers
of marriage bitter.

And one fine morning
you impatiently chose
sweet freedom,
like a schoolchild.

Today dressed as a pirate,
you can be seen in bars
with six lovers to a side
—Isabel, young Isabel—

standing tall on a stool,
radiant, your hair tousled
by a wind all your own,
presiding over the revelry.

Who, by the end of a night,
have you not fallen in love with
for the sake of falling in love?
And they have told me everything.

Have you not learned, innocent girl,
that in the third person
beautiful feelings
make dangerous stories?

They do not understand
the sincerity with which
you have given yourself,
young Isabel. Be careful.

For we are in Spain.
For they are one and the same:
the fools who are your lovers,
the brute who is your husband.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Sometimes I Remember...
translations.text:
Sometimes I remember
certain June nights of that year,
almost blurred, from my adolescence
(it was, I think, nineteen
forty-nine),
because in that month
I always felt a restlessness, a small anguish,
like the heat just beginning,
nothing more
than a particular resonance in the air
and a vaguely tender state of mind.

Those nights were incurable,
and so was the fever.
The late hours of a student alone,
and the untimely book
beside the balcony flung wide open (the street,
just watered, vanished
below among the lit-up foliage),
without a soul to bring to my lips.

How often I remember
you, distant
nights of June; how often
tears came to my eyes, tears
from wanting to be more than a man; how I wanted
to die,
or dreamed of selling myself to the devil,
who never listened to me.
But life also
holds us fast precisely because
it is not what we expected.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Nostalgie de la Boue
translations.text:
New arrangements of the night,
sordid exercises taken from dictation, lessons in desire
that I learned, a pirate,
O young blue-eyed pirate.

In echoing streets the darkness
still had the same complete thickness
I remember from childhood.
And dramatic shadows, cloaked
in the allure of prostitution,
came beside me from a hell
greasy and stifling as an engine room.

Long final hours
in worlds furnished
with tarnished sanitary ware
and wreaths stained with permanganate!
Like a worker polishing a part,
like a knife-grinder,
to make love slowly, biting one's lips.

And to feel oneself dying for every hair's breadth
of pleasure, and to cause pain.

The yellowish light, the staircase
trembling throughout with whispers, my steps,
were still an extension
that exalted me,
like the smell on my hands
—or, on emerging, the cold of dawn, as intense
as the memory of a sensation.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.

translations.title: Even If Only for a Moment
translations.text:
Even if only for a moment, we want
to rest. We dream of letting ourselves go.
I do not know, but somewhere,
provided life lays down its thorns.

A moment, perhaps. And we turn
back toward the deceptive past closing
over the same present fear, which day by day
we knew even then.

One soon

forgets, forgets the sweat of so many nights,
the nervous anxiety that sours the finest achievement,
bringing us to it already exhausted
with nothing but the emptiness of arrival,
the strange indifference of what is already done.

So whenever this fear,
the eternal fear that wears our face,
assails us, we cry out and summon the past
—summoning a past that never existed—

so we may at least believe we truly lived,
and that life is more than this immense,
dizzying pause
when our own vocation, that on which
we once founded our being,
the name we gave our dignity,
we see was nothing more
than a desolate desire to hide.
translations.editorial_note: Direct translation; no separate editorial review was conducted.
